extracted.intended_audience: independent inventors, small businesses, and first‑time patent applicants (U.S.)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, step‑by‑step how‑to for inventors who want to prepare, file, prosecute, and monetize a U.S. patent application (regular or provisional) without necessarily using outside counsel. Covers invention documentation, searching, drafting specification and claims, filing, prosecution, foreign filing, and post‑issue matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to patents and other intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides an overview of patents and other forms of intellectual property to frame what protection is available and how it differs from other IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as foundational background to decide whether patent protection (versus other IP) is appropriate; page lists this as the opening chapter title (no further detail on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: The science and magic of inventing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the inventive process itself—how inventions are created and the practical aspects of developing ideas into inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter title suggests material on inventing practices and mindset; page does not include chapter text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation: the DDP and the PPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain thorough documentation of the invention (DDP) and understand the role and use of a provisional patent application (PPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the importance of documenting development and using the PPA as an option; listed as a chapter heading 'Documentation, the DDP, and the PPA'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will your invention sell?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the commercial potential of an invention as part of deciding whether to pursue patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter heading indicates guidance on marketability and commercial viability considerations prior to investing in patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is it patentable?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the invention meets patentability requirements (i.e., whether it qualifies for patent protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter title 'Is it patentable?' implies discussion of key patentability standards (novelty, nonobviousness, utility) though specifics are not reproduced on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and you may find (prior art searching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a prior‑art search to identify existing patents and publications that may affect patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 'Search and you may find' denotes instruction on how to search and interpret prior art before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: What should I do next? (filing strategy and decision points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide the next procedural and strategic steps after initial assessment and searching (e.g., proceed to draft, seek counsel, license, or abandon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter title indicates coverage of decision points and options based on prior findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to draft the specification and initial drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a complete patent specification and supporting drawings that disclose the invention sufficiently for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 'How to draft the specification and initial drawings' signals prescriptive drafting guidance (structure, content, and illustration standards) though the page does not include the chapter text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Now for the legalese—the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft clear, properly‑structured patent claims that define the legal scope of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter dedicated to claims drafting; implies guidance on claim scope, dependent/independent claims, and claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finaling and mailing your application
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the formalities to finalize and submit a patent application to the USPTO (forms, fees, formatting, and proper submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 'Finaling and mailing your application' indicates procedural checklist material for filing; specifics not shown on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to market your invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies and practical steps for marketing an invention to potential licensees, manufacturers, or investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter heading suggests content on commercialization and outreach; no detailed guidance on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going abroad (foreign filing strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations and procedures for filing patent applications outside the United States (foreign filing, PCT, priority claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 'Going abroad' implies coverage of international filing routes and timing but details are not visible on this listing page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting the PTO to deliver (prosecution and responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage prosecution before the USPTO, including responding to office actions and advocating for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter title 'Getting the PTO to deliver' signals instruction on interaction with the patent office and prosecuting an application toward grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your application can have children (continuations/divisionals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand continuation, divisional, and continuation‑in‑part practice and when to file child applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 'Your application can have children' indicates guidance on post‑filing family strategies; page shows only the chapter title.

rubrics_metrics.name: After your patent issues: use, maintenance, and infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Post‑issuance topics including paying maintenance fees, exploiting the patent, and enforcing rights against infringers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter title lists key post‑grant responsibilities and enforcement considerations; the page does not include the chapter content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership, assignment, and licensing of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and manage ownership and transfer/licensing of patent rights (assignments, licenses, and related documentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final chapter heading indicates coverage of legal transfer and licensing mechanics for inventions; specifics not provided on this page.
